{
"Design Pattern": "A reusable, generalized solution to a commonly occurring problem within a given context in software design, serving as a template that can be adapted to solve specific design challenges.",
"Factory Pattern": "A creational design pattern that abstracts and encapsulates the process of object creation, allowing clients to instantiate objects without specifying their concrete classes.",
"Observer Pattern": "A behavioral design pattern in which an object (the subject) maintains a list of dependents (observers) that are automatically notified of state changes, enabling loose coupling between interacting objects.",
"Strategy Pattern": "A behavioral design pattern that defines a family of interchangeable algorithms and encapsulates each one, allowing an object's behavior to be selected and varied at runtime.",
"Singleton Pattern": "A creational design pattern that restricts the instantiation of a class to a single instance and provides a global point of access to it.",
"Creational Pattern": "A category of design patterns that deal with mechanisms of object creation, aiming to create objects in a manner suitable to the situation while hiding instantiation logic.",
"Structural Pattern": "A category of design patterns concerned with how classes and objects are composed to form larger structures, facilitating flexible and efficient object composition.",
"Behavioral Pattern": "A category of design patterns focused on communication, interaction, and the assignment of responsibilities between objects to achieve flexible and maintainable behavior.",
"Object Creation": "The process of instantiating objects from classes in object-oriented programming, including the allocation of memory and initialization of state.",
"Object Composition": "A design principle in which complex objects are built by combining or assembling simpler objects, enabling reuse and flexibility over inheritance.",
"Loose Coupling": "A design quality in which components or objects have minimal dependencies on one another, promoting modularity, maintainability, and ease of change.",
"Instantiation": "The act of creating a concrete instance (object) of a class, allocating resources and initializing its state according to the class definition.",
"Runtime Behavior": "The actions, decisions, and interactions performed by a software system during its execution, which may vary dynamically based on inputs or configuration.",
"Software Design Problem": "A recurring challenge or issue encountered during the design of software systems, typically addressable through established design principles or patterns.",
"Reusable Solution": "A general, proven approach or template that can be applied across multiple contexts to solve similar problems, reducing duplication of effort and improving consistency."
}
